newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end within whisker of record high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end within whisker of record high.

text.p: Dutch shares ended Monday within a hair's breadth of a record closing high, climbing at the outset on a 78-point Wall Street gain on Friday but slipping back in the last hour as the New York market stalled.
The AEX index closed 6.07 points up at 652.76, off the day's high of 654.40 and a fraction short of the 652.84 closing record set on January 6. The 654.61 all-time high was set the same day.

"I should say there was a pretty good chance of a new record this week," said one dealer. Some in the market, however, were worried that signs of volatility on Wall Street could be signalling the start of turbulent trading elsewhere.

"Wall Street last Friday was pretty wild," said one dealer, referring to Wall Street's higher closing on Friday after falling nearly as much at the opening. The Dow by the Dutch close was pretty much unchanged after a strong start on Monday.

"If you look at all this volatility around I think it shows that the institutions don't really want to get involved," said one dealer, adding, "Volume's not that great...and a lot of it is related to the derivatives markets.
"Every now and then when a company comes with merger and acquisition news or a new year statement everyone jumps on that stock -- otherwise they keep to the sidelines," he continued.

Technical analysts say the AEX is meeting intermediate resistance at 652.50, while the January 6 all-time high of 654.61 is seen as the major resistance. Chartists also highlight volatility in the markets, advising a neutral stance.

One dealer said he believed open interest in the options market pointed to a large number of AEX index options expiring on Friday at around the 650 level, implying that investors would buy in the cash market to defend that level.
"Exposure in the options market is biggest around the 650 level. I think we can get up to 658 and then after that the next stop is 669, although then you'll see profit-taking," he said.
